title: Simulated cells resolve fate ambiguity using context set by other ambiguous cells

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Simulated cells resolve fate ambiguity using context set by other ambiguous cells

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the active-inference simulation, identical undifferentiated cells starting at one location migrate rapidly to their target locations and then differentiate (around the eighth time step) into head, body and tail types as ensemble free energy falls, showing cells can resolve ambiguity about their fate even when it depends on context set by other equally ambiguous cells.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Simulating self-assembly

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: These results are compelling in the sense that they show cells can resolve ambiguity about their fate, even when that resolution depends upon the context established by other (equally ambiguous) cells.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Friston K, Levin M, Sengupta B, Pezzulo G, “Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation”, Journal of the Royal Society, Interface (2015), doi:10.1098/rsif.2014.1383; section “Simulating self-assembly”. Scope: Active-inference simulation of eight cells forming a head–body–tail morphology

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-place-05: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.90

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: All central variables and the decision criterion are explicit model outputs. Independent reruns over seeds can determine whether the described sequence and ambiguity resolution are robust.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run the specified eight-cell simulation from undifferentiated co-located states and record trajectories, fate probabilities, and ensemble free energy. The claim is supported if migration precedes differentiation near step eight and contextual fate ambiguity resolves; otherwise it is refuted.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Exact random seeds are not reported.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.9
data existence: 0.85
operationalizability: 0.95

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Timing, free-energy decline, and fate resolution are direct outputs of a public solver the paper tells the reader to run. A short rerun can match or miss the reported eighth-step differentiation. The test resolves the simulation trajectory, and the current target bitmap is a version caveat rather than a missing method.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-run the published ensemble from a shared undifferentiated start and record migration time, the time step at which cell-type expectations separate, and ensemble free energy. Differentiation far from the reported eighth step, or free energy that does not fall as identities resolve, would refute the reported trajectory.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Identity resolution is read from the model's expectation variables, which are defined by the same generative model.

The current default target mask differs from the 2015 head–body–tail pattern, which can shift timing.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.9
data existence: 0.88
discriminating power: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.72

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In the paper's eight-cell active-inference model started from identical co-located undifferentiated cells, migration toward target locations happens first and fast, differentiation into head/body/tail types follows at around the eighth time step, ensemble free energy falls as identities resolve, and identities end resolved even though each cell's identity depends on signals from other equally ambiguous cells.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered, over 20 random seeds (initial expectations with log precision -4), 32 steps: define migration time t_m as the first step at which the mean distance of cells to their best-assigned target positions falls below 50% of its value at step 0, and differentiation time t_d as the first step at which at least 6 of 8 cells have a most-probable identity of the type encoded at their assigned target and mean max identity probability exceeds 0.5. The claim is supported if, in at least 16 of 20 runs: t_m < t_d; t_d lies in [4, 16] (within a factor of 2 of the reported eighth step); ensemble free energy at step 32 is below step 1; and at step 32 mean max identity probability exceeds 0.5 with at least 7/8 cells correctly typed.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: in fewer than 10 of 20 runs the conditions hold, or in the majority of runs differentiation precedes or coincides with migration (t_d <= t_m), or the median t_d is outside [2, 24] or never reached. Between 10 and 15 qualifying runs is 'mixed'.
